data.title: We Like The Quality Of Attendo's (STO:ATT) Earnings
data.description:
Investors signalled that they were pleased with Attendo AB (publ)'s (STO:ATT) most recent earnings report. This reaction by the market reaction is understandable when looking at headline profits and we have found some further encouraging factors.

We've found 21 US stocks that are forecast to pay a dividend yield of over 6% next year. See the full list for free.

Zooming In On Attendo's Earnings

As finance nerds would already know, the accrual ratio from cashflow is a key measure for assessing how well a company's free cash flow (FCF) matches its profit. To get the accrual ratio we first subtract FCF from profit for a period, and then divide that number by the average operating assets for the period. This ratio tells us how much of a company's profit is not backed by free cashflow.

That means a negative accrual ratio is a good thing, because it shows that the company is bringing in more free cash flow than its profit would suggest. That is not intended to imply we should worry about a positive accrual ratio, but it's worth noting where the accrual ratio is rather high. To quote a 2014 paper by Lewellen and Resutek, "firms with higher accruals tend to be less profitable in the future".

Over the twelve months to September 2026, Attendo recorded an accrual ratio of -0.16. That indicates that its free cash flow quite significantly exceeded its statutory profit. To wit, it produced free cash flow of kr2.3b during the period, dwarfing its reported profit of kr1.02b. Attendo's free cash flow improved over the last year, which is generally good to see.

That might leave you wondering what analysts are forecasting in terms of future profitability. Luckily, you can click here to see an interactive graph depicting future profitability, based on their estimates.

Our Take On Attendo's Profit Performance

Happily for shareholders, Attendo produced plenty of free cash flow to back up its statutory profit numbers. Based on this observation, we consider it possible that Attendo's statutory profit actually understates its earnings potential! Better yet, its EPS are growing strongly, which is nice to see. The goal of this article has been to assess how well we can rely on the statutory earnings to reflect the company's potential, but there is plenty more to consider. With this in mind, we wouldn't consider investing in a stock unless we had a thorough understanding of the risks. data.title: Is Earnings Guidance Reset Altering The Investment Case For nLIGHT (LASR)?
data.description:
• nLIGHT reported third quarter 2026 revenue of US$73.76 million and a net loss of US$7.18 million, and issued fourth quarter guidance calling for US$84 million to US$90 million in revenue with a defined split between Products and Advanced Development.
  • The latest update highlights that supply chain constraints are limiting how fully nLIGHT can convert defense and advanced program demand into earnings, even as year to date revenue reached US$236.54 million with a smaller loss than the prior year period.
  • We will now look at how nLIGHT's revenue guidance and ongoing supply chain friction could influence the broader investment narrative.
Spot potential peers to nLIGHT's directed energy and defense exposure by scanning our curated list of list of solid balance sheet and fundamentals (24 results).

nLIGHT Investment Narrative Recap

To own nLIGHT, you need to be comfortable with a story built around directed energy, sensing and defense programs, and a business that is still reporting losses while it scales. The analyst consensus Narrative on Simply Wall St leans heavily on execution of large laser weapon and sensing contracts and on the shift away from legacy cutting and welding. Recent guidance shows demand in place but also highlights that supply chain friction and Chinese component scrutiny are still the key operational drag.

The short term swing factor remains how quickly nLIGHT can turn its award backlog and Advanced Development work into higher margin Products revenue as supply chains ease. The biggest current risk is that component constraints and regulatory checks persist or broaden, keeping product gross margin in the guided 34% to 40% band and limiting how much of that directed energy pipeline shows up in earnings, while the firm is still absorbing the revenue headwind from exiting older industrial markets.

The most relevant fresh datapoint is the fourth quarter 2026 outlook for US$84 million to US$90 million of revenue, with about US$63 million from Products and US$24 million from Advanced Development at the midpoint. That split matters if you are watching how quickly nLIGHT can lean its mix toward higher volume laser hardware tied to programs like HELSI 2, DE M SHORAD and the Joint Laser Weapon System. The analyst consensus Narrative on Simply Wall St highlights these programs as central to the long term thesis.

data.title: The Strong Earnings Posted By Zaptec (OB:ZAP) Are A Good Indication Of The Strength Of The Business
data.description:
Zaptec ASA's (OB:ZAP) earnings announcement last week was disappointing for investors, despite the decent profit numbers. Our analysis says that investors should be optimistic, as the strong profit is built on solid foundations.

We've found 21 US stocks that are forecast to pay a dividend yield of over 6% next year. See the full list for free.

Zooming In On Zaptec's Earnings

In high finance, the key ratio used to measure how well a company converts reported profits into free cash flow (FCF) is the accrual ratio (from cashflow). The accrual ratio subtracts the FCF from the profit for a given period, and divides the result by the average operating assets of the company over that time. You could think of the accrual ratio from cashflow as the 'non-FCF profit ratio'.

Therefore, it's actually considered a good thing when a company has a negative accrual ratio, but a bad thing if its accrual ratio is positive. That is not intended to imply we should worry about a positive accrual ratio, but it's worth noting where the accrual ratio is rather high. Notably, there is some academic evidence that suggests that a high accrual ratio is a bad sign for near-term profits, generally speaking.

For the year to September 2026, Zaptec had an accrual ratio of -0.72. That implies it has very good cash conversion, and that its earnings in the last year actually significantly understate its free cash flow. To wit, it produced free cash flow of kr394m during the period, dwarfing its reported profit of kr141.9m. Zaptec shareholders are no doubt pleased that free cash flow improved over the last twelve months.

That might leave you wondering what analysts are forecasting in terms of future profitability. Luckily, you can click here to see an interactive graph depicting future profitability, based on their estimates.

Our Take On Zaptec's Profit Performance

As we discussed above, Zaptec's accrual ratio indicates strong conversion of profit to free cash flow, which is a positive for the company. Because of this, we think Zaptec's underlying earnings potential is as good as, or possibly even better, than the statutory profit makes it seem! Furthermore, it has done a great job growing EPS over the last year. The goal of this article has been to assess how well we can rely on the statutory earnings to reflect the company's potential, but there is plenty more to consider. In light of this, if you'd like to do more analysis on the company, it's vital to be informed of the risks involved. Case in point: We've spotted 1 warning sign for Zaptec you should be aware of.

data.title: What Siemens Shareholders Got Right
data.description:
Analysts spent late 2025 arguing over whether Siemens was roughly fairly priced, with one set of assumptions pointing only slightly above the market price and another pointing below it. For Siemens shareholders, the return over the past year was 23.9%, including dividends. If you had been weighing those conflicting fair values on 13 November 2025, what exactly in the record would have justified taking that risk?

A Narrative on Simply Wall St is one investor's written case for a company, with its growth, margin and multiple assumptions spelled out. Those assumptions imply an estimated Fair Value.

The move put Siemens in the middle of this trade. Scan 53 AI infrastructure stocks for other companies exposed to it.

The Two Siemens Stories Investors Had In Front Of Them

The shares cost €227 at the start of the period, and Siemens investors were weighing two very different but plausible stories.

On the bullish side, one Narrative saw Fair Value at €246, 9% above the start price, built on 6.1% annual revenue growth and profit margins reaching 11.2% within about three years.

The more cautious view put Fair Value at €208, 8% below the start price, assuming 5.0% yearly revenue growth, a 17.0% profit margin over five years, and a future P/E of 18.0x.

What The Results Changed For The Siemens Argument

Siemens later reported Q4 2026 revenue of €23,683m and net income of €2,191m, with net margin at 9.3% versus 7.7% a year earlier. That mix of higher sales, higher profit and a wider margin leaned toward the bullish case that expected healthier profitability, although it did not directly test the specific 11.2% or 17.0% margin targets yet.

The useful takeaway is simple. When a thesis hinges on better margins, track net margin alongside revenue and earnings in each report and check whether it is actually creeping toward the level the story needs.

What Siemens' Recent Run Already Prices In

Siemens trades at €279 after a 23.9% gain over the past year. The bullish analyst Narrative on Simply Wall St sees Fair Value above that level based on a stronger mix from Smart Infrastructure and industrial software partnerships rather than just broad AI excitement.

The Narrative argues today's price still does not fully credit the possibility that higher margin Smart Infrastructure and Digital Industries cash generation can be sustained while Siemens works through restructuring and Mobility pressure.

"A key factor is that Siemens maintains execution on higher-margin Smart Infrastructure and Digital Industries guidance, while turning its record backlog and data center orders into sustained free cash flow growth despite restructuring costs and Mobility headwinds."

Not everyone reads the same price the same way. → See the higher figure this Narrative lands on, and how it gets there

Siemens And The Power Behind It

Siemens puts equipment and software inside factories, trains and data centers. Nearby, another industrial player concentrates on the electricity that keeps everything running.

Your chips, sensors and drives are useless if power is unstable. This other business focuses on generation hardware and control systems that help support dependable supply.

It also sells transformers, grid gear and software that move electricity from plant to plug. That matters as AI projects and electrification plans demand tougher, smarter grids.

The puzzle for you is simple. If Siemens stands to benefit when industry spends on automation, who stands to benefit when the grid itself must scale to match?
